paragraphs: Universal approximation asks whether an architecture can represent functions in a target class to arbitrary accuracy. This paper develops a shared framework for studying that question across transformer architectures. It extends ideas previously used for residual networks to models with attention, reducing the need for an entirely separate proof for each architectural variation.

The framework identifies the ability to distinguish tokens as a fundamental requirement and supplies a general sufficient condition for universal approximation. When the attention layer satisfies an analyticity assumption, checking that condition becomes substantially simpler. The resulting argument is non-constructive: it establishes representational capability without providing a procedure for building the required approximating model.

The authors apply the framework to several attention mechanisms, including kernel-based and sparse attention. Their results extend earlier guarantees and cover architectures that previous work did not address. They also illustrate how the framework can guide designs with particular functional symmetries. These are guarantees about expressive capacity; the central contribution is a more unified way to establish them.
neurips-2025-a-unified-framework-for-est.tldr: A unified theoretical framework establishes universal approximation guarantees for a broad range of transformer architectures under sufficient conditions.

paragraphs: Video fusion combines complementary visual information into a single video. Processing each frame independently can produce individually useful images whose appearance changes inconsistently over time. This paper addresses that mismatch with UniVF, a framework that explicitly uses neighboring frames to produce informative fused videos with greater temporal coherence.

UniVF combines multi-frame learning with optical flow-based feature warping. Optical flow supplies motion information so that features from different frames can be brought into correspondence. This makes temporal relationships part of the fusion process, rather than treating the video as a collection of unrelated images. The approach targets both the information retained within frames and the consistency between them.

The paper also introduces VF-Bench, covering multi-exposure, multi-focus, infrared-visible, and medical video fusion. Its aligned video pairs come from synthetic generation and curated existing datasets. A shared evaluation protocol measures spatial quality alongside temporal consistency. The authors report state-of-the-art results across all four tasks on this benchmark, supporting the value of evaluating and learning video fusion as a temporal problem.
neurips-2025-a-unified-solution-to-video.tldr: UniVF combines motion-aware multi-frame learning with a four-task benchmark to improve video fusion quality and temporal consistency.

paragraphs: Reconstructing a three-dimensional point cloud from images requires balancing plausible shape structure with agreement with the observations. Some diffusion approaches learn this relationship directly, tying the model to particular conditioning inputs or view counts. This paper instead combines a diffusion prior with likelihood updates that steer reconstruction toward the supplied measurements.

Its main contribution is Forward Curvature-Matching, or FCM, which adapts the size of those updates. Previous methods in this line use fixed, heuristic step sizes that can slow convergence and reduce reconstruction quality. FCM uses forward automatic differentiation and finite-difference curvature estimates to determine step sizes dynamically, making the measurement-fitting component more responsive to the optimization problem.

The resulting method supports single-view and multi-view reconstruction, and can accommodate different input modalities by substituting the measurement operator without retraining. On ShapeNet and CO3D, the authors report better reconstruction at matched or lower numbers of function evaluations, including higher F-score and lower CD and EMD. The findings connect adaptability to improved reconstruction efficiency in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2025-adaptive-3d-reconstruction-.tldr: FCM adapts likelihood-update step sizes during diffusion sampling to improve flexible 3D reconstruction without retraining.

paragraphs: Diffusion image generation repeatedly runs a denoising network, making inference expensive. The computational needs can vary across this process, so applying one uniform acceleration strategy may miss useful differences between timesteps. Another difficulty arises when layers are removed before fine-tuning: pruning decisions reflect weights that will subsequently change.

ALTER addresses both issues by jointly learning which layers to remove, which specialized subnetwork to use at each timestep, and how to fine-tune the model. A trainable hypernetwork produces pruning decisions and routes timesteps to temporal experts while the UNet continues to adapt. This makes model compression and expert specialization parts of one optimization process.

The authors report visual fidelity comparable to the original 50-step Stable Diffusion v2.1 model while using 20 inference steps and 25.9% of its total multiply-accumulate operations. They also report a 3.64-fold speedup with 35% sparsity. These results demonstrate substantial savings in the stated comparison, supporting coordinated pruning and timestep specialization as an effective acceleration approach.
neurips-2025-alter-all-in-one-layer-prun.tldr: ALTER jointly optimizes layer pruning, timestep routing, and fine-tuning to accelerate diffusion generation while preserving reported visual fidelity.

paragraphs: Variational inference approximates a target probability distribution using a more manageable family of distributions. Highly expressive families, including normalizing flows, often have theoretical assurances that depend on reaching an intractable global optimum. This paper develops variational flows whose convergence guarantees are built around a different construction.

The construction starts from involutive Markov chain Monte Carlo kernels. The authors represent these kernels as invertible, measure-preserving systems of iterated random functions, then use those functions as flow maps. This yields three new variational families with provable convergence in total variation. The recipe supports arbitrary state spaces and is described as tuning-free and asymptotically exact, meaning exactness is a limiting guarantee.

The framework addresses practical restrictions of earlier approaches with related guarantees, including MixFlows, while using substantially weaker theoretical assumptions. Experiments cover posterior approximation, Monte Carlo estimation, and estimation of normalization constants. Across these tasks, the proposed flows match or outperform NUTS and black-box normalizing flows, showing that the convergence-oriented construction can also be practically competitive.
neurips-2025-asymptotically-exact-variat.tldr: The paper constructs tuning-free variational flows from involutive MCMC kernels, obtaining asymptotic convergence guarantees and competitive empirical performance.

paragraphs: A vision-language model's response can depend on image changes that people cannot readily perceive. This paper investigates how precisely such changes can influence generated text. Its theoretical and empirical analysis shows susceptibility to image-based adversarial examples capable of manipulating individual output tokens, making the issue more specific than simply causing an incorrect answer.

The proposed Vision-language model Manipulation Attack, or VMA, optimizes these image perturbations using first-order and second-order momentum techniques together with a differentiable transformation mechanism. The method combines these components to find visual modifications that steer the model's output. The central concern is the degree of control an altered image can exert over language generation.

The authors describe applications spanning jailbreaking, response hijacking, privacy breaches, denial of service, and sponge examples. They also identify a constructive use: injecting watermarks for copyright protection. Evaluations across multiple scenarios and datasets support VMA's effectiveness and generalizability. The findings therefore concern both a model vulnerability and a mechanism that can be used for protective marking.
neurips-2025-attention-your-vision-langu.tldr: VMA shows that imperceptible image perturbations can precisely steer vision-language model outputs, enabling both attacks and watermark injection.

paragraphs: Research on diffusion-model backdoors has produced multiple attacks and defenses, but comparing them fairly requires shared definitions and evaluation procedures. BackdoorDM addresses this evaluation problem. It brings existing methods into a common benchmark so that differences in attack setup or measurement do not remain separate, incompatible research conventions.

The benchmark includes nine attack methods, four defense strategies, and three visualization tools. Its organizing framework distinguishes three attack types and five target types, reflecting the variety of backdoor behavior studied in diffusion models. This classification gives researchers a common language for specifying what an attack attempts to produce and how a defense should be assessed.

The authors also summarize evaluation metrics for the different types and propose a unified evaluator based on a multimodal large language model. They conduct a comprehensive evaluation using the framework. The contribution is an infrastructure for systematic comparison and analysis: combining implementations, categories, metrics, and visualizations makes it easier to examine diffusion-model vulnerabilities within one experimental setting.
neurips-2025-backdoordm-a-comprehensive-.tldr: BackdoorDM unifies diffusion-model backdoor attacks, defenses, and evaluation tools in a comprehensive benchmark.

paragraphs: Behavioral cloning learns decision-making by copying demonstrations. Usually, the demonstrator already knows the task well and shows nearly optimal behavior. This paper asks whether withholding some task information can produce more useful demonstrations for generalization. An expert who lacks that information must explore to discover how to complete the task.

The resulting demonstrations include behavior for dealing with uncertainty, which a learner can then imitate. The authors compare cloning these partially informed experts with cloning fully informed experts in real robot peg insertion tasks and Procgen videogames. Their experiments show better generalization to unseen tasks from the blindfolded demonstrations, including settings with limited human demonstrations.

The theoretical analysis supports the empirical pattern: generalization error scales with the square root of I divided by m, where I measures task information available to the demonstrator and m counts demonstrated tasks. Within that analysis, reducing available task information improves the scaling. Together, the results indicate that demonstration design can reduce the number of demonstrated tasks needed for effective generalization.
neurips-2025-blindfolded-experts-general.tldr: Cloning experts who must explore because some task information is hidden improves generalization in the studied robotic and videogame settings.

paragraphs: Answering a standalone programming question differs from helping someone understand a particular project through several conversational turns. CodeAssistBench evaluates that broader form of assistance. Its questions come from actual GitHub issues, and models work with access to the relevant codebase rather than only an isolated problem statement.

CAB automatically builds datasets from issues tagged as questions, with configurable choices such as programming language, repository age, and star count. It also containerizes the codebases and uses simulated users to conduct multi-turn evaluations inside those environments. The reported test set contains 3,286 questions from 214 repositories across seven programming languages, giving the benchmark a range of project-specific contexts.

The evaluated models achieved success rates of 70–83% on Stack Overflow questions but resolved at most 16.49% of CAB issues from repositories created after their training cutoff. This gap indicates that strong performance on standalone questions does not translate directly into project-grounded assistance. CAB's automated construction process also allows the benchmark to expand as new repositories and questions appear.
neurips-2025-codeassistbench-cab-dataset.tldr: CodeAssistBench reveals a substantial gap between answering standalone programming questions and resolving multi-turn questions grounded in real codebases.

paragraphs: Generating a conversation requires more than producing clear speech for each sentence. A system must preserve distinct speakers, handle overlaps, and place utterances at appropriate times. CoVoMix2 addresses these requirements with a fully non-autoregressive framework for zero-shot dialogue generation involving multiple speakers.

The model uses flow matching to predict mel-spectrograms directly from multiple transcription streams, bypassing intermediate token representations. Its training approach includes separating speakers at the transcription level, aligning information at the sentence level, and randomly masking information at the prompt level. These strategies are intended to help the model capture conversational structure while maintaining coherent speaker identities.

The authors report better speech quality, speaker consistency, and inference speed than strong baselines including MoonCast and Sesame. CoVoMix2 does not require a transcript of the prompt, although transcriptions still specify the dialogue to generate. It also supports overlapping speech and precise timing control. These capabilities make the reported advance relevant to controllable conversation synthesis as well as natural-sounding output.
neurips-2025-covomix2-advancing-zero-sho.tldr: CoVoMix2 directly generates multi-speaker speech with flow matching, improving reported quality, speaker consistency, and speed while supporting overlap and timing control.

paragraphs: Dynamic graphs describe systems whose relationships change through time. Their events need not occur at regular intervals, so a useful model must account for both event history and the time separating events. DyG-Mamba treats this challenge as long-term sequence modeling using a continuous state-space approach.

Inspired by the Ebbinghaus forgetting curve, the method uses irregular time gaps as control signals for how much historical information to retain. This gives elapsed time a direct role in updating memory. A second mechanism, inspired by review cycles, changes core parameters so the model can selectively revisit historical information and filter noisy inputs. Together, these mechanisms govern both forgetting and selective retention.

The authors evaluate DyG-Mamba on 12 datasets covering dynamic link prediction and node classification. They report state-of-the-art performance on most datasets, along with substantially improved computational and memory efficiency. The findings support using time-sensitive memory dynamics to model evolving graphs, with gains spanning prediction quality and the resources required to process event histories.
neurips-2025-dyg-mamba-continuous-state-.tldr: DyG-Mamba uses irregular event timing to control memory and selective review, improving dynamic-graph prediction and efficiency across the reported evaluations.

paragraphs: This paper studies how much approximation power can come from the design of activation functions in a shallow network. It examines a single-layer version of XNet, whose activations derive from the Cauchy integral formula. The focus shifts from previously studied deep XNet variants to what this compact architecture can achieve.

The authors establish near-exponential approximation rates for the shallow variant, exceeding the polynomial bounds discussed for multilayer perceptrons and spline-based architectures such as Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks. This theoretical result connects the mathematical form of the activations to expressive power. It supports activation design as an important source of approximation capability beyond increasing network depth.

Empirically, the paper reports over 600-fold lower approximation error on discontinuous functions and up to 20,000-fold lower residuals in physics-informed partial differential equation problems. It also reports improvements in policy accuracy and sample efficiency for PPO-based reinforcement learning, with comparable or better computational efficiency than KAN baselines. These task-specific findings support shallow XNet as a compact option for approximation, scientific computing, and control.
neurips-2025-from-kolmogorov-to-cauchy-s.tldr: Single-layer XNet combines theoretically strong approximation rates with substantial reported gains over KAN baselines across approximation, scientific computing, and control tasks.

paragraphs: Rectified Flows learn vector fields intended to move samples along straight paths between source and target distributions, supporting very few inference steps. This paper examines a failure mode of that objective under deterministic training: the model can memorize arbitrary source-target training pairings instead of learning a transport rule that generalizes.

The authors analyze Gaussian-to-Gaussian transport and compare loss-gradient variance in stochastic and deterministic regimes. Low gradient variance in deterministic training favors memorization. They show that intersecting training paths do not prevent this behavior: a memorizing vector field can exist even at such intersections, and optimization can converge to that ill-defined field. Deterministic integration then reproduces the training pairings.

A particularly direct construction makes every interpolating line intersect, yet inference still recovers the specific pairings used in training. Experiments on CelebA support the analysis: deterministic interpolants induce memorization, while adding small amounts of noise restores generalization in the reported evaluation. The work links a concrete optimization signal, gradient variance, to the distinction between learning transferable transport and reproducing training associations.
neurips-2025-gradient-variance-reveals-f.tldr: The paper links deterministic Rectified Flow training to memorized source-target pairings and shows that small noise restores generalization in its empirical evaluation.

paragraphs: Neural operators learn mappings between functions, such as the mappings involved in solving partial differential equations. This paper connects these models to Gaussian processes, extending a relationship already studied for infinitely wide neural networks. The connection provides a probabilistic description of outputs and a route to reasoning about uncertainty.

The authors establish conditions under which arbitrary-depth neural operators with Gaussian-distributed convolution kernels converge to function-valued Gaussian processes. The conditional nature of this result matters: the connection is derived for architectures satisfying the stated setup. They then show how to compute the resulting covariance functions for two operator parameterizations, one of which is the Fourier neural operator.

Using these covariance functions, the paper computes Gaussian-process posteriors for regression problems, including partial differential equation solution operators. This makes the theoretical relationship usable for inference. It also helps expose the preferences built into Fourier neural operator architectures and offers a foundation for designing different inductive biases in kernel-based methods that learn mappings between functions.
neurips-2025-infinite-neural-operators-g.tldr: Under specified conditions, infinitely wide neural operators induce function-valued Gaussian processes whose covariances support probabilistic operator regression.

paragraphs: Video steganography hides information inside video. Conventional approaches modify existing video content, which can introduce accumulating distortions and make the hidden information detectable. LD-RoViS instead places information into the video-generation process itself, using a deterministic latent diffusion model without additional training.

The method adjusts implicit conditioning parameters during diffusion to create a channel for carrying secret data. This shifts the embedding mechanism away from direct alterations to an existing cover video. Video compression and later processing can still disrupt recovery, so the framework adds a multi-mask mechanism designed to reduce the resulting extraction errors. Those robustness measures address a central difficulty in extending generative steganography from images to videos.

The reported experiments embed approximately 12,000 bits in a five-second video and recover them with accuracy above 99%. This demonstrates a combination of capacity and extraction reliability in the evaluated setting. The contribution is a training-free framework that couples generation-time embedding with explicit protection against errors introduced by video compression and post-processing.
neurips-2025-ld-rovis-training-free-robu.tldr: LD-RoViS embeds data during diffusion video generation without training, reporting roughly 12,000 bits per five-second video with over 99% extraction accuracy.

paragraphs: Generating an interaction involving two people and an object requires coordinating relationships among all three. Distances, poses, and motion depend on the shared situation. This paper formulates that task as Human-Human-Object Interaction generation and develops a text-conditioned framework that models people in relation to each other and the surrounding object.

To supply training material, the authors introduce a captured dataset and a method for synthesizing additional interaction data using image generative models. They extract human-object and human-human interactions as intermediate representations, then train separate text-conditioned score-based diffusion models for those two kinds of relationships. This decomposition lets each model learn one part of the larger interaction.

A unified sampling process combines the two models to generate complete interactions. The framework also extends to settings with more than two people and supports multi-human motion generation involving objects. Experiments report realistic text-conditioned outputs and improvements over earlier approaches focused on single-person human-object interactions. The findings support combining complementary relationship models to generate richer shared activities.
neurips-2025-learning-to-generate-human-.tldr: The paper combines human-object and human-human diffusion models to generate text-described interactions involving multiple people and objects.

paragraphs: A single model serving several prediction objectives may need more capacity than separate models solving each task individually. That extra capacity can increase the amount of data needed to learn good trade-offs. This paper asks when unlabeled data can reduce that statistical burden in semi-supervised multi-objective learning.

The first result establishes an obstacle: for some loss functions, the cost of the larger model class remains unavoidable even in an unusually favorable setting. The learner is given the optimal solutions for the individual tasks and the distributions of their inputs. Knowing those individual solutions therefore does not always remove the difficulty of learning a shared compromise.

The picture changes for objectives based on Bregman losses. The authors prove upper bounds showing conditions under which model-class complexity may affect only the unlabeled-data requirement. A simple pseudo-labeling algorithm achieves these bounds. The contribution is a distinction between loss-dependent barriers and opportunities: unlabeled examples can substantially reduce labeled-data needs in the identified settings, but the advantage does not hold for every objective.
neurips-2025-on-the-sample-complexity-of.tldr: The paper identifies when unlabeled data can absorb the complexity cost of multi-objective learning and when that cost remains unavoidable.

paragraphs: PBR-SR improves low-resolution textures used in physically based rendering by drawing on a pretrained image super-resolution model. The challenge is that enhancing rendered views independently can produce inconsistent details across viewpoints or make the result sensitive to lighting. The method therefore refines a shared set of texture maps through multiple rendered views.

It iteratively reduces differences between super-resolution guidance and differentiable renderings, then transfers the improvements back into the texture maps. Constraints across views help reconcile the image model's suggestions into shared textures. Additional identity constraints operate directly on the PBR maps to keep the enhanced result faithful to the low-resolution input. No extra training or new training data is required.

The authors evaluate both artist-designed and AI-generated meshes, reporting better results than directly applying super-resolution models and earlier texture-optimization approaches. Improvements appear in evaluations of the PBR textures and their rendered appearance. This combination matters because useful texture enhancement must support the material representation as well as its images, including applications where the object is relit.
neurips-2025-pbr-sr-mesh-pbr-texture-sup.tldr: PBR-SR uses pretrained image super-resolution guidance and multi-view optimization to refine mesh material textures without additional training.

paragraphs: An embodied agent can acquire new skills or improve existing ones over time, but this creates a compatibility problem. A higher-level policy may rely on an earlier organization of those skills. If the repertoire changes, the policy's chosen subtasks may no longer connect cleanly to the behaviors that execute them.

SIL-C introduces an interface that keeps these two spaces aligned. It uses a bilateral mapping based on lazy learning to connect the subtask space referenced by policies with the skill space that produces agent behavior. For each subtask, the framework selects a suitable skill using similarity between trajectory distributions. This lets the interface account for an evolving repertoire.

The intended outcome is that improvements in skills benefit downstream policies without retraining those policies or changing their structure. Evaluations across several skill-incremental-learning scenarios show that SIL-C maintains this compatibility while preserving learning efficiency. The paper's contribution is therefore an explicit mechanism for keeping reusable high-level decision-making connected to lower-level capabilities as those capabilities develop.
neurips-2025-policy-compatible-skill-inc.tldr: SIL-C dynamically maps policy subtasks to evolving skills so downstream policies can benefit from skill improvements without retraining.

paragraphs: A vision-language model may learn a fact through one modality without recalling it equally well through another. This paper studies that cross-modality gap directly. The question matters both for useful knowledge acquisition and for understanding how memorized, potentially sensitive information can be accessed through different kinds of input.

The authors create a synthetic persona dataset containing generated person images and textual descriptions. This gives them a controlled setting for teaching facts through one modality and testing recall through the other. The design separates how well the model remembers information in its original modality from how well that knowledge transfers across modalities.

The experiments show that transfer does occur, but recall in the target modality trails recall in the source modality by a substantial margin. The gap also appears with more capable models, in machine-unlearning settings, and in multi-hop cases. The authors propose a baseline approach to mitigate it. The findings identify cross-modal accessibility as a distinct concern when evaluating what a multimodal model has learned.
neurips-2025-quantifying-cross-modality-.tldr: Controlled persona experiments show that memorized facts transfer between vision and language, but recall remains substantially weaker across modalities.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning can be expensive before it becomes effective, and changing deployed policies or communicating between agents can add further costs. This paper studies those burdens together with regret, the performance loss accumulated during learning. Its setting is on-policy learning in finite-horizon episodic Markov decision processes, including a federated version with multiple agents.

The authors introduce Q-EarlySettled-LowCost and FedQ-EarlySettled-LowCost. They establish a simultaneous combination of near-optimal regret, burn-in costs that scale linearly with the numbers of states and actions, and logarithmic policy-switching or communication costs. Burn-in here measures the sample requirement for reaching near-optimal regret behavior. Earlier methods described in the paper fail to achieve this full combination.

The work also supplies gap-dependent guarantees for regret and switching or communication, matching or improving the best-known bounds. These results are theoretical guarantees within the specified decision-process setting. Their significance is the joint accounting of learning quality, initial data requirements, and operational changes, showing that model-free learning can address all three costs together.
neurips-2025-regret-optimal-q-learning-w.tldr: Two model-free Q-learning algorithms jointly achieve near-optimal regret, linear burn-in scaling, and logarithmic switching or communication costs in the studied setting.

paragraphs: A generated driving video can look convincing while containing geometric distortions that weaken its value as training data. This paper identifies and quantifies that problem through a gap in 3D object-detection performance between synthetic and real data. RLGF addresses it by refining video diffusion models with reinforcement-learning rewards tied to geometry.

The rewards come from specialized autonomous-driving perception models operating in latent space. A windowing optimization method provides targeted feedback during diffusion, while a hierarchical reward system assesses point, line, and plane alignment along with scene occupancy coherence. The authors also introduce GeoScores to measure geometric distortions. These components connect generation quality to spatial properties relevant to downstream perception.

In applications including DiVE on nuScenes, the paper reports a 21% reduction in VP error and a 57% reduction in depth error. It also reports a 12.7% improvement in 3D object-detection mAP, narrowing the real-data performance gap. The findings support geometric feedback as a way to improve both synthetic video structure and its usefulness for perception.
neurips-2025-rlgf-reinforcement-learning.tldr: RLGF uses perception-based geometric rewards to improve synthetic driving videos and narrow the reported downstream 3D detection gap.

paragraphs: Generating realistic graphs requires preserving global structure as well as relationships among individual nodes and edges. Connected components and loops are examples of properties that can be overlooked when a model concentrates on the joint distribution of nodes and edges. TAGG brings these topological characteristics into diffusion-based graph generation.

The method uses persistent homology to represent structural information and incorporates it through two components. A Persistence Diagram Matching loss encourages generated graphs to retain the desired topology. A topology-aware attention module guides the denoising network toward the homological characteristics of the original graphs. One component shapes the training objective, while the other influences how the network processes structural information.

Experiments on conventional graph benchmarks report strong generation performance across multiple metrics and closer agreement with the original distribution of topological features. An application to real brain networks further demonstrates potential for complex graph data. The results support explicitly modeling topology when the goal is to reproduce the large-scale organization of graphs as well as their local connections.
neurips-2025-topology-aware-graph-diffus.tldr: TAGG incorporates persistent-homology losses and attention into graph diffusion to better preserve global topological structure.

paragraphs: Giving a vision-language model external knowledge by appending image and text tokens can greatly lengthen its context and sometimes hurt performance. This paper investigates a more compact memory representation: dense embeddings that carry multimodal and multilingual knowledge. Its central idea is to adapt a vision-language model to serve as the memory encoder itself.

The proposed CoMEM method fine-tunes only 1.2% of the model's parameters using 15.6 thousand self-synthesized examples. The adapted encoder represents supplied knowledge in eight continuous embeddings. The vision-language model that uses this memory at inference remains frozen, allowing the memory component to be integrated when needed without updating that inference model.

The authors report improved performance on complex multimodal reasoning and evaluate the approach across eight benchmarks. The findings support compact learned representations as a useful alternative to long sequences of external knowledge tokens. The contribution combines a representation choice with an efficient adaptation procedure: the model's existing capabilities provide the foundation for turning varied knowledge into a small, reusable memory input.
neurips-2025-towards-general-continuous-.tldr: CoMEM adapts a vision-language model to encode external knowledge into eight embeddings, improving reported multimodal reasoning with a frozen inference model.

paragraphs: Recognizing handwritten mathematics requires understanding both individual symbols and their spatial arrangement. Handwriting variation makes similar characters hard to distinguish, while longer expressions create additional consistency challenges. Uni-MuMER addresses these issues by fully fine-tuning a pretrained vision-language model without changing its architecture.

The method combines three training tasks aimed at different sources of recognition error. Tree-Aware Chain-of-Thought develops structured spatial reasoning about expressions. Error-Driven Learning targets confusion between visually similar characters. Symbol Counting encourages consistency in long expressions. Together, these tasks inject mathematical handwriting knowledge into a general-purpose model through its training data and objectives.

Experiments on CROHME and HME100K report performance beyond the compared specialized and vision-language models. The abstract gives improvements of 16.31% over SSAN and 24.42% over Gemini2.5-flash under the stated zero-shot setting. The broader finding is that coordinated, domain-specific training tasks can produce strong recognition results within an unchanged model architecture, bringing layout reasoning, character discrimination, and counting into one fine-tuning framework.
neurips-2025-uni-mumer-unified-multi-tas.tldr: Uni-MuMER combines spatial reasoning, error-driven learning, and symbol counting to improve handwritten mathematics recognition through VLM fine-tuning.
